clinician.trajectory_summary: A 41-year-old man presented with worsening headache, nausea, and photophobia for 3 days without meningeal signs or neurological symptoms. On admission, characteristic vesicular rash in the V2 trigeminal distribution on nose and hard palate was noted. CSF analysis showed pleocytosis with lymphocytic predominance, elevated protein, and normal glucose. PCR testing detected VZV DNA in the CSF, confirming VZV meningitis. The patient was treated with intravenous acyclovir for 14 days with symptom improvement.
